source.title: HiDe-LLaVA: Hierarchical Decoupling for Continual Instruction Tuning of Multimodal Large Language Model
source.authors: Haiyang Guo; Fanhu Zeng; Ziwei Xiang; Fei Zhu; Da-Han Wang; Xu-Yao Zhang; Cheng-Lin Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study measures layerwise CKA similarity across task-trained representations and reports shared similarity in lower layers but a notable decrease at the top layer, refining the scope of convergence.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the layerwise CKA comparisons in Section 4.1 and Figure 1. The task-performance tables and ablations of HiDe-LLaVA are not results about representation convergence and are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The CKA analysis (Sec 4.1, Appendix B) compares layer outputs of one base model, LLaVA-v1.5-7B, on inputs from different instruction datasets after LoRA fine-tuning. It measures how similar features are across tasks within one model family. It does not compare independently trained models, architectures, seeds or modalities on shared inputs, and has no scale sweep. It is a motivation for a continual-learning method and does not bear on convergence of representations across models. It cites Kornblith et al. for CKA but neither original source. No relation value fits exactly; it neither tests nor uses the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that, across tasks, layers below the top encode similar general knowledge and the top layer is task-specific. They use this to motivate fusing lower-layer LoRAs and expanding the top-layer LoRA as an MoE. Note that the comparison is across task inputs and LoRA variants of a single base model, not across independently trained models.
record.recipe_differences: Uses layerwise output CKA comparisons across instruction-tuning tasks; it does not test a scale-dependent convergence trend across independently trained models.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported CKA pattern differs by layer; the study also describes an example task-pair comparison, but does not report a systematic comparison of alternative metrics or metric settings.

fits_no_version.finding: In LLaVA-v1.5-7B LoRA-fine-tuned on six instruction datasets, linear CKA between layer outputs on different task inputs is relatively high below the top layer. It drops markedly at the top (32nd) layer, even for dissimilar tasks like IconQA vs Flickr30k.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within one pretrained MLLM fine-tuned on different tasks, lower-layer representations stay task-general while the top layer becomes task-specific.

record.problems: The relevant CKA findings are qualitative in the text, with no numerical values or uncertainty reported. The analysis does not compare alternative similarity measures, test scaling, or establish why the lower-layer similarity occurs.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant CKA result omitted. Task-performance results and method ablations were left out because they evaluate continual-tuning performance or efficiency rather than representation convergence.

untested.parts: No comparison of independently trained models, no scale or capability sweep.
No vision-language alignment on paired data as models improve.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation tests.
No feature- or circuit-level comparison across models.
Only linear CKA is used. No alternative metrics, settings or OOD inputs are varied for a convergence measurement.
Only LoRA variants of one base model are compared. No plateau or cause (shared data or objectives) of cross-model alignment is tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' with V6 and V7 supports is wrong. V6 concerns metric and data dependence of cross-model convergence. V7 concerns incomplete convergence of independently trained models. Neither is measured here. All verdicts are removed. This is a continual-instruction-tuning method paper; Tables 1–4 and Figs 2, 4–8 are method performance and correctly omitted.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep, and no comparison of independently trained models across architectures, objectives, or training data as model size or capability increases.
Does not measure alignment between vision and language models on paired images and captions as either model improves.
Compares task-trained representations, not networks trained from different initializations; does not test shared features or subspaces across seeds.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
Does not test whether the same interpretable features or circuits recur across models.
The study reports layer- and task-related CKA comparisons, but does not compare alternative similarity measures or their settings, nor report out-of-distribution tests.
Reports partial similarity across layers, but does not test whether alignment plateaus with scale or whether shared training data or objectives explain it.

rows.subject: LLaVA-v1.5
rows.stage_stated: LoRA fine-tuned on six instruction-tuning datasets
rows.operation_detail: Compared output CKA similarity at the same layers across different instruction-tuning datasets.

conditions.value: bottom and middle layers versus top layer

rows.measure: Output CKA similarity between task representations at corresponding layers
rows.value: Similarity is relatively high in layers below the top layer and markedly lower at the top layer.
rows.note: The paper describes this as an aggregate pattern across tasks; it does not provide numerical CKA values in the text.
rows.check: Appendix B defines X_i, Y_i as layer-i outputs for two different task inputs. These are LoRA variants of the same LLaVA-v1.5-7B base, not independently trained models compared on the same inputs. No metric choice or OOD manipulation is varied, so the row says nothing on V6 or V7. Values are qualitative only (Fig 1 heatmaps).

rows.subject: LLaVA-v1.5
rows.stage_stated: LoRA fine-tuned on IconQA and Flickr30k
rows.operation_detail: Compared output CKA similarity at the same layers for IconQA and Flickr30k task representations.
rows.measure: Output CKA similarity between task representations at corresponding layers
rows.value: The similarity difference is notable only at the top layer; similarity remains relatively high across the other layers.
rows.note: The text describes this named task pair qualitatively; numerical values are not stated.
rows.check: Same issue as R1. It is the IconQA vs Flickr30k pair within one fine-tuned base model, so it measures task-input similarity, not cross-model convergence. No numeric values are given.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CKA comparisons across the tested task representations and layers
reader_labels.reason: The reported similarity pattern differs by layer, with a marked decrease at the top layer (R1, R2); alternative metrics and out-of-distribution inputs were not tested.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Task-trained LLaVA-v1.5 representations, lower layers compared with the top layer
reader_labels.reason: The results describe relatively high similarity in lower layers alongside more task-specific divergence at the top, indicating partial rather than complete convergence (R1, R2).
